title: Costs rebuild 2: one record per model request, summed
description:
Repos: **JKershaw/LinearViewer** (Harbour) and **JKershaw/simple-dispatcher** (the runner).

**Goal.** Every model call's tokens and cost are tracked simply and reliably, in code that is easy to maintain (LIN-3936). This step makes what is recorded complete and per request, so the one cost read from rebuild 1 has the right thing to read.

**Context.**

* The LIN-4126 review, `docs/reviews/cost-tracking-review-2026-11-02.md`: §3.1 item 1 ("a usage record is one model request"), §5 (the simplest reliable design, and why it beats repair alone), and findings F2, F3 and F10.
* `docs/plans/costs.md`: decision 3 (pricing) and decision 4 (one read model).
* LIN-4176's close-out: the one read (`lib/cost-read.js`) and its figure rule, priced sum plus coverage, never $0 for unknown.
* The note after tidy 5 on LIN-3936: four product choices about which issue a cost counts under, which all "point to the per-request ledger, where each call can carry the issue it was for, rather than more rules".
* Related tickets this step may absorb: LIN-3859 (subagent tokens), LIN-3948 (the final usage post at session end and reap).

**This step, and why now.** Rebuild 1 gave every surface one read. But what the read sums is still a snapshot per session: a running total from the runner's hook, from runner-kit and from opencode, each folded its own way. So:

* a Haiku 5.5 session that crosses the long-context threshold prices to nothing;
* subagents aren't counted;
* a mixed-model session is priced at one model;
* the last turns of a one-turn or killed session can go unreported;
* every reader still has to know which harness reports cumulatively.

Harbour's own calls already have one record per request (the call log). This step brings the runner's work to the same shape: one record per model request, posted once, summed. That lets per-request pricing apply the provider's tiers as the provider does, and lets a call carry the issue it was for. It is next because the read is now in one place, so changing what it reads is one change.

Not here: the Costs page; changing which issue a cost counts under (that's John's call, made later, once each request can carry its issue); estimating sessions that never reported anything.

**Done when.**

* Every model request a runner session makes, subagents included, is recorded once in Harbour. Posting it again changes nothing.
* The one read sums those records, and every figure follows from them. No reader needs to know whether a harness reports running totals.
* A Haiku 5.5 session that crosses the long-context threshold gets a price, and a mixed-model session is priced per model.
* The work of a session that ends after one turn, or is killed or reaped, is still counted.
* On recorded inputs, figures before and after differ exactly where the change list says: nothing differs that isn't on it, and everything on it is seen to differ. (A list that only allows differences passes a reverted fix; that happened in rebuild 1.) The recorded inputs hold each case a witness depends on. On live data, the share of runner work that Harbour can price is measured before and after and reported.
* Old snapshot rows still read correctly, or the change list says how they're treated.

**Permission.** It may remove things: the snapshot path, folds that nothing needs once records are summed, and tests that pin implementation. It may leave bugs for now if it names them. It may split into pieces across the two repos, in whatever order keeps figures right between deploys.

**Report back**, under these headings:

* **What changed**
* **What was left, and why**
* **What still looks fuzzy across the area**
* **Follow-ups**: listed, not filed.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

A Survey looked at the ground first. Its advice, which we're taking:

1. **First, decide where the records live and what Harbour accepts,** and ship that while nothing reads it yet:
   * **How they arrive:** a way to post many records at once. A feedback message is capped at 2000 characters, and one Haiku session made 486 requests.
   * **Posting again:** upsert by request id. Streamed messages grow across lines, so "posting again changes nothing" means keeping the largest value of each field, not insert-if-absent.
   * **Pricing:** it reads the record's own kind, not the harness. Today pricing keys on harness, so a per-request `claude-code` record would still price Haiku over 100k to nothing.
   * **Cutover:** write down the rule for sessions that hold both snapshots and records, so nothing is counted twice.
   * **The call log:** check before reusing it. About 42 places read it as "Harbour's own calls".
2. **Then build a transcript corpus** with Haiku over 100k, a subagent, mixed models, a `<synthetic>` tail, a session killed before its first Stop, and one resumed across the deploy. Record the "before" by running today's runner fold over it.
3. **Only then switch the runner**, with re-sending of anything not acknowledged. The runner chose snapshots on purpose (see the comment in its hook): a delta on a fire-and-forget post under-reports forever.
4. **Switch the read last.**

Rulings may be needed along the way. John answers them in the morning, so park a piece rather than guess.

## Implementation Plan

needs multiple sessions

plan-review due: yes

**Implemented as approved (stub written at close-out, 2026-11-04).** The plan's seven pieces landed, plus two recorded splits (LIN-4212 orphan wake-row records; LIN-4226 piece 4b, the read loads its own records). Harbour PRs: [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2267](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2267>), /pull/2273, /pull/2274; runner PRs: [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/323](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/323>), /pull/325. Deviations from the plan are the ones recorded in comments on this ticket: workflow-agent subagent directories (LIN-4199), the amended race-class gate rule (LIN-4200/4201), and post-time coverage. Follow-ups: LIN-4235, LIN-4236, LIN-4237 (and LIN-3493 for F7).

The full plan text (decisions D1..D14, where the behaviour lives, order of landing, replay change list, failure modes, report-back) is preserved in the LIN-4195 task snapshots and the comment trail; the close-out comment records how each ledger item was settled.

comments.body:
### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. The premises hold at HEAD, the design solves the problem the ticket names, and the guards it loosens each have a test. The notes below are corrections the builder can make without changing any decision.

**What I checked** (Harbour `72305215`, runner `cc2650a`, both still HEAD of main; neither repo has a commit since the ticket was created):

- **Pricing premise is true.** `computeUsageCostUsd` returns null on `crossesThreshold && isRunningTotal(usage)` (`lib/model-pricing.js:368`), and `isRunningTotal` keys on the reported harness (`lib/row-usage.js`). D5 targets the actual cause.
- **The cutover's superset argument holds for runner lineages.** A follow-up always resumes the original session's harness and transcript (`SD:dispatcher.js` "resuming never switches engines"; a missing transcript fails the resume instead of starting a fresh session). So a lineage is one claude-code transcript, the same thing today's last-wins fold already assumes.
- **Deriving the anchor from the posting row is sound.** `doc.rootItemId = item.rootItemId || doc._id` is set when the row is created, inherited via `followUpTo` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:727`), and `anchorOf` reads it.
- **Reap and cancel flushes pass the ownership rule.** `addFeedback` filters on `status:'taken'` (`lib/dispatch-store.js`). History rows stay `taken` after the session ends; only undone queue rows become `cancelled`. So D10's late posts reach the row.
- **The runner-token twin route is already gated.** `/api/proxy/runner/*` sits behind the path-scoped `requireGrant('take')` (`routes/proxy-runner.js:12`).
- **The store operations work in dev and tests.** MangoDB implements `$max` and `bulkWrite`, and `lib/kpi-daily-rollup.js` has the E11000 retry precedent for concurrent upserts.
- **The subagent layout is confirmed on this host.** Files sit at `~/.claude/projects/<proj>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`. Every usage line I sampled carries `message.id` and `requestId`, and lines repeat per message id, so per-field max is needed.
- **Reader census.** The read's callers at HEAD match D13: `routes/proxy-compute.js`, `lib/model-routing-spend.js`, `lib/effort-readout.js`, `lib/terminal-marked-task-cost.js`, `lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js` (+ `lib/weekly-budget.js` via its `lineageRecords` output), `lib/run-view.js`. One direct snapshot reader is missing from the list (note 1).

**Blocking findings:** none.

**Notes for the builder**

1. **The /kpis harness disclosure shares are a reader of running-total semantics that D13 does not list.** `lib/terminal-marked-task-cost.js:99-104` (`harnessReadingOf`) reads each member's snapshot via `usageStateOf(member).usage` and calls `isRunningTotal`, which produces `opencodeSummedShare` and `unknownHarnessShare`. Those are published by `lib/kpi-stats.js` → `lib/render-kpis.js` and pinned in `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/goldens.json`.
   - The D13 census checks only that `readCost`/`lineageRecords`/`lineageFigureOf` get `requestRows`, so it would not catch this.
   - After piece 6, new lineages carry no `[usage]` entry, so `unknownHarnessShare` drifts toward 100% on the public page.
   - Broaden D13's description from "callers of the read" to "every reader of snapshot usage outside the legacy fold": `usageStateOf`, `usageOf`/`lastUsageEntry` (`lib/dispatch-lineage.js`), `readRowUsage`/`readUsageEntry`, and `isRunningTotal`.
   - For a record-read lineage, derive the harness from its records, and decide what `opencodeSummedShare` means once records exist. It is a caveat about the legacy delta fold, so a record lineage is "not delta-summed".
   - Add the share movement to the piece-4 change list, or assert it as a control. Today, record-only corpus case (e) would show up as an unlisted diff.
   - The other hits (`lib/digest-feedback.js` `kpiUsageEntry`, `lib/kpi-stats.js:460`) only feed the legacy fold's aggregation input and can stay.
2. **Make `requestRows` a required argument, not only a census rule.** The ticket's constraint is that a missed caller must not silently fall back to snapshots. A read that throws on `requestRows === undefined` enforces this at runtime too. Keep the census test for anything outside the read.
3. **`incomplete` (the narrow rule) for a record lineage.** D6/D7 don't say how `missingCanChangeFigure` applies once a lineage reads from records. Records are fetched by anchor, independent of which rows the caller fetched, so a missing row cannot change a record figure. State that `incomplete` is false for a record lineage, or give the rule you choose. Otherwise the replay will settle it by accident.
4. **opencode native cost vs read-time price.** D2 stores optional native `costUsd`, and D5 says price at read, but neither says which wins. Today `lib/session-telemetry.js:464` prefers native. Keep that precedence for records, and say so in D5 so opencode figures don't move on the change list unintentionally.
5. **Piece 3's "agree to the cent" filter.** Records include tail turns recovered at reap/cancel (D10), which the last Stop snapshot never saw. For the to-the-cent comparison, restrict to lineages whose last record is at or before their last snapshot. Otherwise, expect `records ≥ snapshot` and report the excess as the L4 recovery. Without this the gate will fail on the fix it is meant to measure.
6. **Ledger size on the runner.** The live `state/sessions.json` is 1.58 MB for 141 sessions and is rewritten on every `updateState`. A `{requestId: fingerprint}` map at roughly 100–500 entries per session would about double it, and records persist 7 days (LIN-4172). Keep the ledger compact (one short hash per id) or in a per-session side file. Either still satisfies D9, since correctness never depends on the ledger.
7. **D7/D10 residue wording.** Transcripts live under `~/.claude/projects/…`, not in the clone, so a clone reap (24 h) does not remove them. The real loss modes are:
   - Claude Code's own transcript cleanup;
   - the 7-day record pass deleting the session record that holds `transcriptPath` (`locateTranscript(sessionId)` is the existing fallback);
   - a host change.
   Run the reap flush at the terminal transition, not at the 7-day record pass.
8. **Lines without `message.id`.** `walkUsage` keys these as `line:${i}`, but D4 rejects a missing `requestId`. None appeared in the transcripts I sampled. Either skip such lines and count the skips in the oplog, or fall back to the entry's top-level `requestId`. Don't post a synthetic per-line id; it would not be stable if a transcript were rewritten.
9. **Mixed-harness lineages under D7.** `foldLineageUsage` documents mixed lineages as additive (opencode deltas + claude-code total). SD never switches harness on resume, so none should arise from the runner. Still, between piece 4 and piece 5 a lineage holding opencode delta rows and claude-code records would drop the opencode spend under "records win". Either add a corpus control asserting that no live lineage mixes harnesses, or scope the cutover per harness (snapshots of harness H are ignored when the lineage has records of harness H). The second is one line in the same function.
10. **The label change in (b) is a product choice.** Labelling a mixed-model lineage by its cost-dominant model moves lineages between groups on Models and the effort read-out. It is correctly on the change list. Name it in the report-back so John sees it, since he owns those groupings.
11. **D4's 2M bound only catches large cumulative totals.** A cumulative total from a short session would pass it. That is acceptable as a guard, because the runner side is what prevents posting totals (the D9 walk is per message). Keep the runner witness that its records sum to the oracle, not just the intake rejection test.

**Shape:** multi-session across two repos, as stated. The 0→1→2→3→4 order keeps figures right between deploys, and piece 3 is a real gate. Filing pieces as sub-issues at the start is right.

### Breakdown

LIN-4195 is split into the seven pieces from its approved plan. The plan-review Approve is comment `eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1`, rev 1. Each piece is one PR. Each carries its slice of the plan and the plan-review notes that apply to it.

| Piece | Ticket | Repo | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 · corpus + baseline goldens | LIN-4197 | both | — |
| 1 · Harbour intake, store, per-record pricing (D1–D5) | LIN-4198 | Harbour | LIN-4197 |
| 2 · runner posts claude-code records; Stop/reap/cancel flush; subagents (D9–D11) | LIN-4199 | runner | LIN-4198 |
| 3 · live measurement gate (records vs snapshots, volume) | LIN-4200 | Harbour (data) | LIN-4199 |
| 4 · the read sums records, cutover, required `requestRows` (D6, D7, D13) | LIN-4201 | Harbour | LIN-4200 |
| 5 · opencode + runner-kit post records (D12) | LIN-4202 | both | LIN-4198 |
| 6 · stop posting snapshots; re-measure; final report-back | LIN-4203 | both | LIN-4201, LIN-4202 |

**Why the order and the edges:**
- **0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4** is the plan's chain. Pieces 0–2 move no figure. Piece 2 needs piece 1's route deployed first. Piece 3 is the gate for piece 4. Piece 4 diffs against piece 0's goldens, which piece 0 records before any read change.
- **5 follows 1** and is independent of 2–4. By D7, its lineages read from snapshots until they hold records.
- **6 needs both 4 (live and measured) and 5**, so that no producer is left posting only snapshots.

**Session fit:** each piece fits one session. The plan already cut the multi-session, two-repo job to one PR per piece, and each piece is verified before the next one starts.

**Where the review notes went:**

| Review note | Piece |
|---|---|
| 1 (harness shares read snapshots) | piece 4 |
| 2 (required `requestRows`) | piece 4 |
| 3 (`incomplete` is false for record lineages) | piece 4 |
| 4 (native `costUsd` wins) | pieces 1 and 4 |
| 5 (to-the-cent filter) | piece 3 |
| 6 (compact ledger) | piece 2 |
| 7 (reap flush at the terminal transition) | piece 2 |
| 8 (lines without `message.id`) | piece 2 |
| 9 (mixed harness) | control in piece 0, decided in piece 4 |
| 10 (label change is John's call) | named in pieces 4 and 6 |
| 11 (runner records sum to the oracle) | piece 2 |

**Staleness check:** no commit to either repo since `72305215` / `cc2650a`, and every cited file exists. One drift was found: the stale sidechain comment the plan cites at `SD:transcript.js:411-414` is now at `:432-435`. LIN-4199 carries the corrected reference.

**LIN-4197 (piece 0) PRs:** runner https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/312 (head `7a2d83c`), Harbour https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2264 (head `73c5a990`). Both open, not merged.

Two drifts the plan should know about before piece 3 and piece 4:

**(a) LIN-4126's `measure.mjs` double-counts a shared message id.** It parses each file on its own, so a message id present in both the main transcript and a subagent transcript is priced twice. On the subagent case it gives $0.0895 (main $0.0563 + subagent $0.0332), against the deduplicated oracle of $0.0752. D11 is right that the shared id is one request. Any live comparison in piece 3 has to dedupe the same way, or it will show a false gap. `walkUsage` itself does not double count: given main and subagent lines together, it counts the id once and matches the oracle exactly.

**(b) `goldens.json` is paired with `expected-changes.json`, so piece 4's baseline diff must run against `goldens-lin4197.json`.** `goldens.json` is the LIN-4177 baseline (`9e397e6b`). At HEAD the replay already differs from it in 114 paths, and those are the listed changes. Re-recording it would erase them and break W9, so it is byte-identical in the Harbour PR. The HEAD baseline (existing corpus, each LIN-4197 stage, and the mixed-harness control) is the sibling `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/goldens-lin4197.json`, recorded by `record-lin4197.mjs`. `scripts/cost-replay.mjs --record` still rewrites `goldens.json` and must not be run without re-baselining the change list.

**Plan correction from LIN-4199 (piece 2), merged as simple-dispatcher `9478e1c`.** D11 names `<session-dir>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl` as the subagent transcript location. That is incomplete: Workflow-tool agents write to `<session-id>/subagents/workflows/wf_*/agent-*.jsonl` (beside a `journal.jsonl`), and those files carry billed assistant usage. The runner now walks both (top-level first, then workflow directories, sorted; `journal.jsonl` and `*.meta.json` not read). Any later piece that reads subagent transcripts (piece 5, opencode/runner-kit, and piece 3's comparison) should use both locations.

## Autopilot status, LIN-4195 (2026-11-04)

**Done and verified (PRs merged, CI green on merged commits, tickets Done):** LIN-4197 piece 0, LIN-4198 piece 1, LIN-4199 piece 2, LIN-4202 piece 5.

**Blocked on a person: LIN-4200 (piece 3, the gate before the read switches).** It needs read-only access to the production linear-viewer Mongo (or a Harbour-host run of its script), plus the workspace urlKey, and about 3 days of records (they exist only since ~05:00Z 2026-11-04). Options: (a) access + wait ~3 days (recommended); (b) access now + a shorter window you name. LIN-4201 (piece 4) is held behind LIN-4200 and LIN-4203 (piece 6) behind LIN-4201, so LIN-4195 cannot complete until this clears. Snapshots keep posting alongside records, so nothing is broken meanwhile.

**Also yours:** (1) the mixed-model labelling change (flagged on LIN-4201, LIN-4203); (2) operator checks not run for lack of prod access: LIN-4198 `getIndexes()` on `request-usage` + live route probe; LIN-4199 doc count for item f6248f11 (~136) + a manual-abort check (flush reason `cancel`, no 404); LIN-4202 three live checks (opencode normal-end, opencode error/hold, runner-kit `runner usage`) after the runner picks up 765289d; (3) LIN-4202's piece-4 cutover-scoping acceptance was NOT discharged (review asked Done to wait; close-out closed under the post-deploy rule) and is carried on LIN-4201.

Accept a shorter window size, and you can use the railway cli to access mongo.

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

## Action needed: rotate the production Mongo root password

While LIN-4200 (piece 3) was setting up live read access via the Railway CLI, the **production Mongo root password for Railway service `MongoDB-harbour` was exposed in a worker session transcript** (worker ROOT `3ccfa072`, 2026-11-04 ~07:15Z). Please rotate it in Railway and update anything that reads it (the Harbour service's Mongo URL). The secret is not repeated here.

**LIN-4200 status:** measurement script + 17 fixture tests done (local commit `23326722`, not pushed). The live run is blocked on ruling `lin4200-railway-ssh`: `MongoDB-harbour` has no public TCP proxy, so the CLI tunnel needs an SSH key registered on the Railway account (or the script run on the Harbour host). The worker session is held and resumes when that ruling is answered. LIN-4201 and LIN-4203 stay held behind it.

File a ticket for John (me) to rotate later.

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

### Piece 3 (LIN-4200): live measurement gate for piece 4. Go/no-go: NO-GO on the to-the-cent rule as written

Branch `feat/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots`, PR #2267 (measurement only, no production change). Commits 23326722, ab23ad51, 49133a53, rebased on main 5334c81a. Full detail and the open decision are on LIN-4200.

**Data and window.** Harbour workspace `linearviewer`, read-only, production.
- Measurement run (records up to 07:46Z): 2,069 request records, 28 lineages with usage, 2 with no usage, 0 orphan records. Runner oplog window from 2026-11-04T04:59:21Z (the LIN-4199 merge).
- First record's first-line time 2026-11-03T19:28:39.924Z, a pre-deploy request posted after the deploy. Last 2026-11-04T07:46:16.501Z.

**To-the-cent subset** (priced snapshot, no subagents, one model, last record at or before last snapshot): 20 eligible.
- 1 agrees exactly.
- 19 are the same-Stop race. Each gap equals exactly the lineage's last record. That record's first line leads the last snapshot by 353 to 460 ms. The snapshot walked the transcript before the final line reached disk.
- 0 unexplained.
- Disclosure: the 2 s race window was chosen after the first live run. The first run had 19 disagreements, all with leads of 0.19 to 0.45 s, and the window was set from those leads. The rule should be re-validated on fresh data.

**Tail and residue.** Records after the last snapshot: 0 in this sample. D7 residue (records below snapshot): 0.

**Shares** (token-weighted over 394.4M snapshot tokens and 405.7M record tokens): the snapshot prices 97.3% of tokens (383.7M). The one lineage it cannot price is a Haiku snapshot over 100k, which records price. Records price 100%. By lineage: snapshot-priced 27 of 28, record-priced 28 of 28.

**Runner oplog** (request-usage.flush, from 04:59:21Z): 136 flush events, posted 2,069, rejected 0, failed 0, deferred 0, skipped.noRequestId 0, request-usage.error 0.

**Case classes.**
- Present: subagents (1 lineage, excluded from the subset), mixed model (6 lineages), Haiku over 100k (1), resumed across the deploy (pre-deploy records present).
- UNMEASURED: one-turn lineage (none in sample), `<synthetic>` tail (skipped at write, not visible in Harbour), killed or reaped with no Stop, reap-flush tail (L4/L5 recovery; no reap-only lineage in sample).

**D13 volume** (production, 07:54Z): 2,319 records over 34 lineages. Per lineage: min 15, median 36, p95 211, max 295. Since the deploy: 320 records per hour.

**explain('executionStats') on the listForAnchors query.** Every case uses IXSCAN on `urlKey_1_rootItemId_1`, no COLLSCAN, keysExamined = docsExamined = nReturned.
- One task: nReturned 128, 1 ms.
- 30-day window (3,969 dispatch anchors): nReturned 2,319, 6 ms.
- Record lineages: nReturned 2,319, 4 ms.
- Scratch at 230,745 records: 242 ms.

**Timings** (5 repetitions, median; production through an SSH forward, so upper bounds):
- `/kpis`: 1,079 ms (972 to 1,203).
- Workspace KPIs: 828 ms (804 to 958).
- Records-sum path, 30-day window: 86 ms (81 to 90).
- Records-sum path, one task: 36 ms.
- Scratch copy on a local mongod: 5,000 records 26 ms; 50,000 249 ms; 200,000 1,048 ms; 230,745 1,177 ms (1,144 to 1,209). Fit about 5.3 µs per record, and it predicts the steady measurement within 3%.
- Projection basis: 320 records per hour since deploy, times 720 hours, is 230,745. That rate covers 2.9 h and includes some backlog. It agrees with the review's ~100k per 13 days.

**D13 verdict** (thresholds judged by me: 1 s for an uncached page read at steady state, 0.5 s maximum added by piece 4).
- `/kpis` is not too slow. It is stale-while-revalidate (`lib/kpi-page.js`, 60 s), so only the background refresh pays, about 2.3 s at steady state. No fallback needed.
- Workspace KPIs is too slow if the records path runs on every load: 0.83 s today plus about 1.2 s, roughly 2 s. Piece 4 needs caching the page as `/kpis` does, or the D13 pre-summing fallback (untimed). I would try caching first.

**Go/no-go for piece 4: NO-GO on the to-the-cent rule as written.** The reason is that 19 of 20 eligible lineages disagree. The disagreements are explained by the same-Stop race, not a pricing or record error, so the rule cannot pass as written.

**The parent plan's assumption is false at Stop.** The plan treats "last record at or before last snapshot" as proof that the snapshot covers that record. That does not hold. A snapshot walks the transcript at Stop, and the final request's first line can land after that walk while its record posts a moment later. Evidence: the gap equals exactly that record's tokens in all 19 cases.

**Recommended path** (the rule amendment is John's decision, open as `lin4200-to-cent-rule` on LIN-4200; I have not decided it):
1. Amend to-the-cent to exclude the named race class, then re-measure on fresh data. The 2 s window was set after the first run.
2. Measure the reap-flush tail, which this sample does not contain.
3. Cache the workspace KPI page as `/kpis` does, or pre-sum non-override models per D13, then time the result.

**Repeatable commands** (paths under `scripts/`; none contain secrets).
- `scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs [--url-key KEY] [--out FILE]`. Needs a read-only `MONGODB_URI`. Optional `LIN4200_WINDOW_START` and `LIN4200_OPLOG`. Tests: `node --test tests/unit/lin-4200-measure.test.js` (21 pass).
- `scripts/lin-4200-d13-volume-timing.mjs [--scale-local] [--out FILE]`. Needs `MONGODB_URI` (read-only) and, for `--scale-local`, `MONGODB_SCRATCH_URI` on loopback only. Optional `LIN4200_REPS` and `LIN4200_TASK`. Tests: `node --test tests/unit/lin-4200-d13.test.js` (11 pass).
- Route to production: the URI is obtained through the hosting platform's CLI and an SSH port forward to the Mongo service, set in the environment at run time and never written to disk.

### Piece 3 follow-up (LIN-4200): ruling applied, gate re-measured. Go/no-go for piece 4 on the amended rule: GO, with conditions
